Axalta Coating Systems Ltd Plans Major Expansion in Bermuda to Meet Rising Global Demand

Axalta Coating Systems Ltd, a leading player in the chemicals industry, announced plans on Thursday for a significant expansion of its operations in Bermuda, signaling confidence in long-term demand for industrial coatings worldwide. The company confirmed a multi-million dollar investment aimed at upgrading its existing manufacturing facility outside Hamilton and expanding its local workforce by more than 50 positions over the next two years.

The expansion, set to commence in the third quarter of 2024, will focus on enhancing production capacity for Axalta’s high-performance coatings used in automotive, marine, and industrial applications. The company cited increasing orders from clients in North America, Europe, and Asia, as well as the growing adoption of advanced coatings in infrastructure and energy sectors.

"With global demand for innovative coating solutions on the rise, Bermuda’s strategic location and skilled workforce make it an ideal base for our growth ambitions," said Martin Fisher, Axalta’s Vice President of Global Operations. "This investment will allow us to better serve our customers and partners, while creating quality jobs and contributing to the local economy."

The Bermuda Chamber of Commerce welcomed the announcement, highlighting the chemicals sector’s growing role in diversifying the island’s economy. “Axalta’s expansion signals the strength of Bermuda as an industrial hub and is a positive development for local suppliers and service providers,” said Chamber CEO Angela Outerbridge.

Axalta did not disclose the total value of the investment, but company representatives indicated that it would include both equipment upgrades and the construction of additional warehouse and laboratory space. Local officials expect the project to generate opportunities for Bermudian contractors and engineering firms. “We are committed to ensuring the economic benefits reach a broad cross-section of the community,” noted Minister of Industry and Commerce, Terrence DaCosta.

Analysts at Confluence Advisory said the move reflects robust global trends in the chemicals sector. “With infrastructure spending accelerating in key markets, demand for specialized coatings is forecast to grow steadily through 2027,” said senior analyst Priya Shah. “Axalta’s decision positions it well to capitalize on this momentum.”

The company expects the expanded facility to be fully operational by early 2026.
